title: Independence of polynomial embeddings for a fixed affine morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. For any two closed immersions $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_S$ and $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_S$ over $S$, where $n,r\geq0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-affine-space], $Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $\mathbf A^n_S$ if and only if $Rj_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $\mathbf A^r_S$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No quasi-coherence of the cohomology of $E$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, comparison of two embeddings of a fixed affine morphism

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and $Q=R[y_1,\ldots,y_r]$. By the affine descriptions in [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] and [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i,j$ correspond to surjections $\alpha:P\twoheadrightarrow A$, $\beta:Q\twoheadrightarrow A$. Choose $f_b\in P$ with $\alpha(f_b)=\beta(y_b)$ and $g_a\in Q$ with $\beta(g_a)=\alpha(x_a)$. Put $T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_r]$. The evaluation surjections $u:T\to P$, $y_b\mapsto f_b$, and $v:T\to Q$, $x_a\mapsto g_a$, give closed immersions $s:\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}T$. On every generator, $\alpha u=\beta v$; hence $si=tj=:h$. This also covers an empty list of variables.

source.place: Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, proof: common polynomial ring and diagram

proof.text: For the graph $u$, identify $T=P[y_1,\ldots,y_r]$ by the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] (the maps fixing every variable are inverse), and put $h_b=y_b-f_b\in T$. For $0\leq b\leq r$, evaluating $y_1,\ldots,y_b$ at $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ induces $T/(h_1,\ldots,h_b)\cong P[y_{b+1},\ldots,y_r]$: evaluation kills each $h_c$, and conversely $p-p(f_1,\ldots,f_b,y_{b+1},\ldots)$ lies in $(h_1,\ldots,h_b)$ since $y_c^k-f_c^k=h_c\sum_{l<k}y_c^{k-1-l}f_c^l$; at $b=r$ the induced map is $u$. On $P[y_{b+1},\ldots,y_r]=C[y_{b+1}]$ with $C=P[y_{b+2},\ldots,y_r]$, multiplication by $h_{b+1}=y_{b+1}-f_{b+1}$ is injective: the top $y_{b+1}$-coefficient of a nonzero polynomial reappears one degree higher in its product, with no domain or nonzero-ring hypothesis. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular], with $R=M=T$ and the list $h_1,\ldots,h_r$, gives $H_q(K_\bullet(h_1,\ldots,h_r))=0$ for $q\neq0$. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], $K_0=T$, $d_1(e_b)=h_b$, every $K_q$ is finite free and $K_q=0$ for $q>r$; so $H_0=T/(h_1,\ldots,h_r)\cong P$ via $u$, and $K_\bullet$ placed in cohomological degrees $-r,\ldots,0$ is a bounded finite-free $T$-resolution of the evaluation module $P$. The same argument with $T=Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, the equations $x_a-g_a$ and $v$ gives a bounded finite-free $T$-resolution of $Q$. For $r=0$ (resp. $n=0$) the resolution is $T=P$ (resp. $T=Q$) in degree $0$.

source.place: Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular) and Tag 0622/0623 (Koszul complex); the polynomial graph instance asserted in more-morphisms.tex Tag 09VC, final paragraph ('straightforward to prove directly')

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] in rank one, the associated sheaves of $P$ on $\operatorname{Spec}P$ and of $Q$ on $\operatorname{Spec}Q$ are their structure sheaves. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec] to $u$ and $v$ identifies $s_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}P}$ and $t_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}Q}$ with the associated $T$-module sheaves of the evaluation modules $P$ and $Q$. Their degree-zero complexes are pseudo-coherent by [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion]: each evaluation module is quasi-isomorphic to the bounded (therefore bounded-above) finite-free resolution of step 2. This use of the affine criterion concerns only these structure modules, not $E$.

source.place: Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, final paragraph: pseudo-coherence of the polynomial graph structure module; perfect.tex Tag 08E7; schemes.tex Tags 01HV and 01I9

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-closed-pushforward-pseudocoherence] to $s$ and $K=Ri_*E$, and to $t$ and $K=Rj_*E$. Step 1 gives the required closed immersions, and step 3 verifies their pushed-forward structure modules are pseudo-coherent. The result gives, at the same integer $m$, $Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent if and only if $Rs_*Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, and $Rj_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent if and only if $Rt_*Rj_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The cited result applies to all derived objects: neither $Ri_*E$ nor $Rj_*E$ needs quasi-coherent cohomology.

source.place: Tag 09VC, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, final paragraph, invoking perfect.tex Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: The composition isomorphisms of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] and the equality $si=tj=h$ identify both $Rs_*Ri_*E$ and $Rt_*Rj_*E$ with $Rh_*E$ in $D(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}T})$. The condition of [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] is invariant under such an isomorphism: compose each local strictly perfect approximation with the restricted isomorphism, whose cohomology maps are isomorphisms, preserving the isomorphisms above $m$ and the surjection in degree $m$. Thus the two equivalences in step 4 have the same right-hand condition, and yield the asserted equivalence.
